Rashi on Menachot 8a:1:1.hebrew: ואם איתא - דדם לא קידש לחצאין, לילף מנחה מדם:
Rashi on Menachot 8a:1:1.english: And if it is so - That blood is not sanctified in halves, let [Rabbi Elazar] derive [the law of a] meal offering from blood.

Rashi on Menachot 8a:1:2.english: From which he removed a handful in the Sanctuary is valid - Even though its law is [to be performed] in the courtyard, like other sacrifices.

Rashi on Menachot 8a:1:3.hebrew: שכן מצינו בסילוק בזיכין - דהיא בהיכל, אלמא דאיכא קמיצה בהיכל, דסילוק היינו קמיצה:
Rashi on Menachot 8a:1:3.english: As we find regarding the removal of the bowls - Which is [performed] in the Sanctuary, indicating that there is taking of the handful in the Sanctuary, for removal is [the equivalent of] taking the handful.

Rashi on Menachot 8a:3:1.english: Before he dismantled it - [Referring to] the arrangement of the showbread on Shabbat.

Rashi on Menachot 8a:3:2.hebrew: הלחם פסול - דהויא לה מנחה שחסרה קודם קמיצה, ואמרינן לקמן (מנחות דף ט:): מן המנחה, פרט לשחסרה. ובלחם הפנים גופיה אמר לקמן (מנחות דף יב:): [קדש קדשים] היא, שאם נפרסה אחת מחלותיה, כולן פסולות:
Rashi on Menachot 8a:3:2.english: The bread is unfit - For it is [considered] a meal offering that became lacking before the removal of the handful, and we say later (Menachot 9b): "From the meal offering" — excluding [a meal offering] that became lacking. And regarding the shewbread itself, [the Gemara] says later (Menachot 12b): "[It is most holy] — it is," that if one of its loaves was broken, all of them are unfit.

Rashi on Menachot 8a:3:3.hebrew: משפרקה נפרס לחמה הלחם פסול - אף ע"ג דלאחר סילוק (מצה) נפרס, פסולה; דהוי שירים שחסרו בין קמיצה להקטרה, ואמרינן לקמן (מנחות דף ט:) דאע"ג דמקטירין קומץ עלייהו, שיריים אסורים באכילה:
Rashi on Menachot 8a:3:3.english: Once he detached it, [if] its bread broke, the bread is disqualified - Even though it broke after the removal (of the matzah), it is disqualified; for it is [considered] remnants that became lacking between the removal of the handful and the burning [on the altar], and we say later (Menachot 9b) that even though they burn the handful on their account, the remnants are forbidden to be eaten.

Rashi on Menachot 8a:3:4.english: And he burns the bowls on its account - [That we do not] derive [it] from a meal offering.

Tosafot on Menachot 8a:1:1.hebrew: ואם איתא לילף מדם - וא"ת: והא בדם ליכא מתוך, והכא איכא מתוך; ובשאר מנחות משמע דמודה רבי אלעזר דאין קדושה לחצאין, כיון דלא קרבין לחצאין? ומיהו יש לפרש, דדם נמי קרב לחצאין, שיש ד' מתנות וז' הזאות דפרה, שכל אחת עבודה בפני עצמה; ושיעור טבילה דלעיל לאו למעוטי חצי הזאה, אלא שיהא בכלי שיעור ז' הזאות. והא דאמרינן (בסמוך) גבי הפריש חצי עשרון ודעתו להוסיף, דאמר רב אינו קדוש, [ופריך]: ואי כרבי אלעזר ס"ל לילף מחביתין — מצינו לפרש, דחשיב ליה דעתו להוסיף כמו טעמא דמתוך, וקדוש לחצאין; ועוד, דאפילו ליכא מתוך בשאר מנחות, מ"מ כיון דקדשי חביתין לחצאין מאיזה טעם שיהיה, ילפינן שאר מנחות מינייהו. אי נמי, הא דנקט רבי אלעזר טעמא דמתוך, משום דרבי יוחנן נקטיה: דאפילו פלגיתו בשאר מנחות, בחביתין אודו לי מיהת מטעם מתוך:
Tosafot on Menachot 8a:1:1.english: And if it is so, let him derive [it] from blood - And if you say: But with blood there is no [rationale of] "mitokh" [that since it is offered in halves, it is sanctified in halves], whereas here [regarding the griddle-cakes] there is "mitokh"; and regarding other meal offerings, it implies that Rabbi Elazar concedes that there is no sanctification in halves, since they are not offered in halves? However, one can explain that blood, too, is offered in halves [i.e., in parts], as there are four applications [of blood on the altar] and seven sprinklings of the [red] heifer, each one of which is an act of service in its own right; and the "measure of dipping" [mentioned] above was not to exclude half a sprinkling, but rather [to require] that there be in the vessel a measure of seven sprinklings. And as for that which we say (nearby) regarding one who set aside half a tenth [of an ephah] and his intention was to add [to it], where Rav said, "It is not sanctified," and [the Gemara] objects: "And if he holds in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, let him derive [it] from the griddle-cakes!" — we can explain that [the Gemara] considers "his intention to add" like the rationale of "mitokh", and [thus] it is sanctified in halves. And furthermore, even if there is no "mitokh" in other meal offerings, nevertheless, since the griddle-cakes are sanctified in halves—for whatever reason that may be—we derive other meal offerings from them. Alternatively, that which Rabbi Elazar formulated the rationale of "mitokh", he formulated it on account of Rabbi Yoḥanan: [namely,] "Even if you disagree regarding other meal offerings, in [the case of] the griddle-cakes at least concede to me on account of the rationale of 'mitokh'!"

Tosafot on Menachot 8a:1:2.hebrew: מנחה שנקמצה בהיכל כשרה שכן מצינו בסילוק בזיכין - ואם תאמר: אמאי לא קאמר כדי שלא יהא טפל חמור מן העיקר, כדאמר בסמוך גבי שלמים ששחטן בהיכל, וגבי כהנים נכנסין בהיכל ואוכלים קדשי קדשים ושירי מנחות? י"ל, דהתם כתיב (ויקרא ג) פתח אהל מועד, (שם ו) בחצר אהל מועד; שייך למימר שלא יהא טפל חמור מן העיקר, לפי שתלה הכתוב באהל מועד:
Tosafot on Menachot 8a:1:2.english: A meal offering from which a handful was taken in the Sanctuary is valid, for so we find with the removal of the bowls - And if you say: Why does he not say [that it is valid] so that the secondary [area] should not be more stringent than the primary [area], as [the Gemara] says nearby regarding peace offerings that one slaughtered in the Sanctuary, and regarding priests who enter the Sanctuary and eat offerings of the most sacred order and the remainders of meal offerings? One can say: There, it is written: "the entrance of the Tent of Meeting" (Leviticus 3), [and] "in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting" (ibid. 6); [therefore] it is applicable to say that the secondary [area] should not be more stringent than the primary [area], since the verse made [it] dependent upon the Tent of Meeting.
